title: Al-Awwal, the First
tomorrow: her hands were raw from the mill. what did her father give her?

lines: THE FIRST MINUTE OF THE DAY.
cards: A café before sunrise: the key in the lock, the alarm, the lights, the first machine starting to hum. Some owners keep a ritual for that first minute.
Yesterday's question was what Muslims say before the first word of anything. One word does it: bismillah. In the name of God.
In full, it's the line that opens the Qur'an, in Pickthall's words: "In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful."

teach.b: Bismillah isn't only for prayer. In Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, tells a boy at the table to say it before he eats.
Doors, car rides, a test, a hard text: ordinary beginnings are where it goes. And the reason sits in today's Name. Al-Awwal, the First.
The Qur'an puts it in one verse with three more Names, which the next three days will open: "He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things."
A du'a of the Prophet in Sahih Muslim spells out the first of them: You are the First, and there is nothing before You.

So bismillah at the start of something small is a big thing: it puts the First first. Here's a detail to tell a friend tonight: the Qur'an itself opens with the same words, so the book starts where the café does.
Now look back at this week from there. The Unique, whom all need. The Able, the All-Powerful.
The one who brings forward and the one who puts back.
Every one of them was already there before the first thing happened. Before your alarm. Before the café lights.

how: Muslims say bismillah before eating, traveling, studying and other everyday beginnings; the Qur'an itself opens with it.

o: the Leader, who goes ahead of His people
the Oldest of all created things
the First, with nothing before Him

games.q: this week's Names — tap the pairs.

s: bismillah is said only before prayer and reading the Qur'an
it opens ordinary things too; the Prophet taught a boy to say it before eating.
one verse names Allah the First, the Last, the Outward and the Inward
"He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward."
Al-Awwal means God was the first thing to be made
the Prophet's du'a says: You are the First, and there is nothing before You.

games.q: your friend is about to send a hard text to her mom and asks how Muslims start something like that. what fits Al-Awwal?
o: begin with bismillah: put the First first, then write the text.
wait until the words are perfect; the First deserves a perfect start.
bismillah is for worship only, so a text doesn't need anything.
games.why: the Prophet taught saying bismillah even before a meal. ordinary beginnings are exactly where the First goes.

practice: Stand up and take a short, slow walk, even just across the room and back. Before the first step, say bismillah, or in the name of God, and let each step after belong to that first word. Then sit for whatever time is left.

wordCard.voice: Al-Awwal. The First, before everything, with nothing before Him: the opening Name of four in one verse.

orig.note: Arabic: the First. it opens the four Names of 57:3.

carryVoice: The line to keep: first, before the alarm and before the first word. That's a week of Names, done.
